title: The Shadow Lines

vibeProfile.oneLine: Across three cities, a family shows how borders cut through real lives.

summary: Moving between Calcutta, Dhaka and London across three generations, Amitav Ghosh's novel follows a narrator piecing together his family's story and the way national borders, drawn on maps, cut through real lives and memories. Circling a violence he only slowly understands, the book meditates on how arbitrary lines create both nations and tragedies. Elegant, non-linear and deeply intelligent, it is one of the finest Indian novels in English and a profound reflection on memory, freedom and belonging.
whyReadIt: Ghosh's elegant meditation on borders, memory and how lines on a map cut through real lives. One of the finest Indian novels.

funFacts.text: It won the Sahitya Akademi Award, India's national literary honour.
